summary.name: Comparison of streaming media software
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia comparison table of about two dozen audio and video streaming server and media software products, covering cost, license, OS support, container formats and protocols.

comparing audio streaming servers for internet radio
checking which streaming protocols a server supports
finding free or open source streaming software
comparing licensing and cost of media servers
checking OS support for a streaming server
summary.what_it_does: The page is a set of comparison tables for streaming media systems, covering both audio and video. Its tables list creator, first release, latest stable version, cost in USD, license, and media type for each product. Further tables show operating system support (Windows, macOS, Linux, Unix), supported container formats (such as MP4, FLV, WebM, MPEG-TS, Matroska) and protocols (such as HTTP, RTSP, RTMP, WebRTC, HLS, DASH, SRTP). A small table compares client synchronization, web interface, GUI and mobile/JavaScript SDK features for a few products. Many cells are marked "?", so the data is incomplete in places.
notable: Side-by-side tables of cost, license, OS support, container formats and streaming protocols for about 22 products
Mixes free open-source servers (Icecast, OvenMediaEngine, Red5) with proprietary ones (Wowza, Ant Media, Unreal Media Server)
Includes encoder and player software such as OBS and VLC alongside servers
caveats: Data is dated; many latest-version entries are from 2006 to 2020, and some products are discontinued or unmaintained (e.g., Windows Media Services, Helix DNA Server)
Many cells are marked '?' (unknown), and the page says it needs more citations
Commercial products list paid licenses (e.g., Wowza, Adobe Media Server, Unreal Media Server) and free developer or trial tiers only
